sentences.text: On the face of record, it appears that the present petitioners are the legal representatives of original Complainant Mr. Salem Mohd. Inamdar, who filed RCC No. 325 of 2017 and prayed for further investigation under Section 153 (3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, in respect of preparation of false and bogus Muntakhab, on which basis the respondent No. 2/accused pretended that, the said document was genuine and on the basis thereof obtained an order of mutation dated 02.02.1982 from the Revenue Authority.
4. The petitioner/Complainant further alleged that respondent No. 2/accused forged the signatures of the deceased Salim Moinoddin Inamdar, the father of witness No. 5.

Though respondent No.
2/Accused had obtained the said order on 02.02.1982, he concealed said fact for a period of 35 years and, all of a sudden, on 04.10.2016, respondent No. 2 submitted an application for mutation before the Tahsildar, Beed, and by suppressing material facts from the Talathi and the Revenue Inspector,
got his name mutated in the revenue record on 25.12.2016, which was a public holiday.

Therefore,
the complainant prayed for an investigation under Section 156 (3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The Complainant filed an affidavit and narrated the facts of the complaint.
5. On 12.06.2017, the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Beed, passed an order directing the concerned Police Station to submit a report under Section 202 of the Cr.P.C.

Accordingly, on 23.03.2018, Shivajinagar Police Station, Beed, made an inquiry and submitted a 4 934criwp1739.20 report stating that, Muntakhab No. 1871 revoked and the accused, who was in possession of Muntakhab No. 4744 not been issued by the Nizam Government.

On the basis of the said Muntakhab the respondent/accused got mutated his name and names of his sibling in 7/12 extract of land of the Darga Hazarat Shaha Kochak Shaha Wali and deleted the name of the Darga Hazarat Kochak Shahawali.

entities.text: Darga Hazarat Shaha Kochak Shaha Wali
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
6. After considering the said report under Section 202 of the Cr.P.C., the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Beed, passed an order on 03.10.2019 and issued process against respondent No.
2/accused for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code.
7. Being aggrieved by the said order, respondent No. 2/accused approached the learned Sessions Judge, Beed, by filing Criminal Revision Application No. 92 of 2019.
On 23.01.2020, the learned Sessions Judge, Beed passed the impugned order and set aside the order of issuance of process dated 03.10.2019 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate.
8. Being aggrieved by the said order, the Original Complainant, through his legal representatives has filed the present petition.

9. Learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners/Complainant canvassed in vehemence that, as per the revenue record, the Dargah Hazrat land and Inam land were vested with the office of the Commissioner, of Archaeology, Hydrabad.

As per the revenue record, 5 934criwp1739.20 Survey Nos. 22 and 95 of village Taraf Pingle were declared as service lands for the Dargah, and corresponding entries to that effect exist in the 7/12 extract.

It is further contended that, as per the revenue record, Muntakhab No. 1871 of the year 1358 Fasli, Muntakhab 1200 San 1320 Fasli,

sentences.text: However, respondent No. 2/accused made scratches in the Original Muntakhab No. 4744 of 1336 Fasli.

He pretended it to be true and on the basis of said Muntakhab, he submitted an application with the Revenue Authorities and obtained an order on 02.02.1982 with ulterior motive showing that, the said land was of the Madat Mash land i.e.
Community land, though in fact it was Khidmat Mash land i.e. Service Land.

Further, respondent No. 2/accused did not disclose the order dated 02.02.1982 for a period of 35 years and thereafter,
for the first time, on 04.10.2016, respondent No. 2/accused, in appendix "A" of the register, with the help of Talathi and Revenue Inspector mutated his name and names of his siblings in 7/12 extract.

10. On the face of record it appears that, in pursuance of order dated 12.06.2017, passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, Shivajinagar Police Station, Beed carried out an inquiry under Section 202 of the Cr.P.C. and submitted report and opined that the Muntakhab No. 1871 of 1358 Fasli has been revoked at the instance of the respondent/accused and the Muntakhab No. 4744 has not been granted by the Nizam 6 934criwp1739.20 Government, which is obtained by the accused on the basis of false and bogus document and also the accused mutated his name and his siblings in the 7/12 extract.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate passed an order dated 03.10.2019 and issued process against respondent No. 2/accused.

However, on 23.01.2020, the learned Sessions Judge, Beed, passed the impugned order holding that, respondent No. 2/accused obtained an order in the year 1982, from the Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition), Beed and after 35 years on 04.10.2016 an application was filed for taking entry in revenue record.

Needless to say that, learned Revisional Court considered the orders passed by Revenue Authority for effecting mutation in favour of respondent No. 2/Accused and those entries have not been challenged by the Complainant.
So also some litigations are pending before the Wakf Board and this Court.

Therefore,
considering the effecting of entries in the name of respondent No. 2/Accused, the learned Revisional Court set aside order dated 03.10.2019, passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate.
However, it is submitted that the Complainant has specifically made allegations about making of false and bogus signatures and preparation of Muntakhab entry No. 4744.
It seems that as per the police report, the document which is possessed by the accused is not issued by the Nizam Government.
Therefore, the question about the genuineness of the said document required to be considered by the trial Court.

The said question about the genuineness of Muntakhab No. 4744, on which basis the Revenue Authority passed an order and taken mutation entry in the 7 934criwp1739.20 name of respondent No. 2/Accused, which is the subject matter of trial.
At this stage, it cannot be concluded that the said document is genuine or forged.

However, the learned Revisional Court passed the impugned order by taking into consideration the only order passed by the revenue authority and effecting revenue mutation entries in favour of respondent No 2/accused without considering the allegations made in the complaint and genuineness of the document.

However, the learned Sessions Court/Revisional Court has taken into consideration only mutation entries made in favour of respondent No.
2/accused on the basis of order dated 02.02.1982.
Therefore, the impugned order passed by the Revenue Court is not justifiable and appears to be of jurisdictional error.
Therefore, the impugned order is liable to be quashed and set aside.

Accordingly, I pass the following order:
